new_statements.translation: Note, however, that there are monosyllabic nouns which place the penultimate tonic accent on the particle [class prefix] that precedes them. In such cases I do not hesitate to write them together. Thus one will look in the dictionary for luto 'spoon' and not to, because the particle lu, taking the tonic accent, may be regarded as part of the word. [p. 25:] Bigni, n. pl. of kigni, written as one word; the particle bears the penultimate tonic accent. — Faces. See kigni. — 2° Dew (accent on the last syllable).

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: The quotation was checked again. Opened (render of PDF p. 12 = printed p. 6 of) and read the page image myself. The p. 6 passage is there verbatim: "Remarquons cependant, qu'il y a des substantifs monosyllabiques, qui mettent sur la particule qui les précède, l'accent tonique de pénultième. Je n'hésite pas, évidemment, à les unir dans ce cas. Ainsi on cherchera dans le dictionnaire luto, cuiller et non pas to, parce-que la particule lu prenant l'accent tonique, peut-être considérée comme faisant partie du mot." (also at line 250 of the, with scanned noise). The p. 25 portion reads in print "Bigni, s. pl. de kigni, s'écrit en un seul mot; la pc. a l'accent tonique de pénult. — Visages. V. ki…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Marichelle treats Vili as having a word-level tonic accent on the penultimate syllable; when the stem is monosyllabic, the penult is the noun-class prefix, which therefore carries the accent and is written together with the stem (lu-to 'spoon', bi-gni 'faces', bi-ka 'beds'). The modern instrumental work (Ndinga-Koumba-Binza 2008) does not describe word stress at all: it treats Civili as a tone language (H/L) and finds only phrase-penultimate vowel lengthening ('in line with a general rule in Bantu languages assigning length to the penultimate syllable of a phrase', p. 164), while referring in passing to 'an unstressed nominal prefix syllable' (p. 30). The 1902 'accent tonique' is most plausibly the Bantu penultimate lengthening/prominence rather than a contrastive stress system.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any source opened.
new_statements.exceptions: Marichelle p. 25 notes a minimal pair bigni 'faces' (accent on penult, i.e. on the prefix) vs bigni 'dew' with 'accent sur la dernière syllabe' — a final-accented word, probably a tonal distinction. Ndinga-Koumba-Binza 2008 p. 146: long vowels (except onomatopoeias) occur only in the first syllable of disyllabic words or the penultimate of polysyllabic words; word-final /a/ is reduced/devoiced (p. 30).
new_statements.domain_note: Marichelle: word level (citation forms of nouns in a dictionary; 'mot' = prefix + stem). Ndinga-Koumba-Binza 2008: lengthening is stated for the penultimate syllable of a phrase- or sentence-final word (phrase level), with tones as the lexical suprasegmental; no word-stress statement.
new_statements.identity_note: Marichelle 1902 describes the Vili of Loango (Congo-Brazzaville coast), the core variety of vili1238; Ndinga-Koumba-Binza 2008 works on Civili of Gabon (Mayumba/Nyanga area; Glottolog codes Civili de Mayumba under vili1238). The 1888 Ussel grammar calls the same Loango variety 'fiote' (not the Kakongo Fiote of Visseq 1889, which is Kongo).

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Ussel 1888 is not wholly free of the word 'ton', contrary to the reader's note: p. 67 (Gallica view 73) 'Est-ce que? Il suffit de changer de ton.' and p. 68 (view 74) 'Ti à la fin de la phrase en prenant un ton particulier. Même chose pour la particule ko' -- these describe sentence-level question intonation, not word stress or lexical tone, so the work stays silent on stress. Nothing else missed; the two not-opened works (Loëmbe 2005, Marichelle 1907) were re-attempted (two downloads each) and remain blocked (403 'Sorry..' on books.google.com; term-cloud-only pages on the new UI); the HathiTrust Ussel copy still returns an automated-access block. sources.note: 'Notions préliminaires' p. 6 (PDF p. 12): Vili has an 'accent tonique de pénultième'; monosyllabic noun stems throw this penultimate tonic accent onto the preceding class particle (luto 'spoon', not to), which is why the prefix is written together with such stems. Entries repeat the rule (p. 25 Bigni 'faces': 'la pc. a l'accent tonique de pénult.'; Bika 'beds': 'La pc. est unie au rad. en raison de l'accent de pénultième'; Bu entry: 'Quand il prend l'accent de la pénultième, nous le laissons uni au subst.') and note one exception: bigni 'dew' has 'accent sur la dernière syll.'
